label: rem:motivic-mass-rationale
title: Why a motivic measure: singular intermediate states and the archimedean realization
html:
The mass endomorphism (proton--electron mass ratio) must assign a finite, q-discrete weight to a Gröbner--Shirshov reduction whose intermediate states are singular: there is no smooth volume form to integrate, no measure-theoretic Lebesgue construction that survives the blow-up. The motivic measure \mu of def:motivic-mass-measure assigns each reduction step a value in the Grothendieck ring \mathcal{M}, purely algebraically, by tracking which classes of varieties appear as exceptional fibers. The categorical analogue of crossing the \chi(A) = -6 topological horizon (topological mass formula) is exactly the contribution [E_i^{\circ}] \mathbb{L}^{-d_i} of the exceptional divisor of that blow-up.

The motivic mass \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta) is a class in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} — a motive, not yet a real number. The real-valued physical mass is recovered by applying the archimedean realization functor, constructed later in this chapter once the adelic substrate it projects from is in place.
